facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm
A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm

concepts.why: The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and presents with a subcutaneous mass and multiple nodules in the liver and lungs, suggesting metastasis.
The patient presents with a subcutaneous mass and multiple nodules in the liver and lungs, which could be consistent with a primary soft tissue sarcoma.
The patient has been treated with regorafenib, which can cause liver injury, and presents with elevated liver enzymes and alpha-fetoprotein levels.
The patient has been treated with sorafenib, which can cause hypothyroidism, and presents with mild anemia and elevated liver enzymes.
The patient has been treated with pembrolizumab, which can cause pneumonitis, and presents with multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules.
The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and presents with elevated liver enzymes and alpha-fetoprotein levels.
The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and presents with elevated liver enzymes and alpha-fetoprotein levels, suggesting underlying liver cirrhosis.
The patient presents with a subcutaneous mass and multiple nodules in the liver and lungs, suggesting metastatic disease.

rationales.F01: The presence of a subcutaneous nodule is more typical of metastatic disease, which could be related to hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis.
rationales.F06: The subcutaneous mass could be related to either hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis or soft tissue sarcoma.
rationales.F10: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels are highly suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules could be related to either metastatic disease or pembrolizumab-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F12: The abdominal CT findings are highly suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis, but could also be related to soft tissue sarcoma or metastatic disease in general.
